name: Florida

windshield.strip: transparent sunscreening strip at the top that does not encroach on the AS-1 portion (FMVSS 205)
windshield.reflective: material must be transparent; no reflectance figure for the strip

frontSide.note: total solar reflectance of visible light max 25% (nonfilm side)

backSide.note: reflectance max 35%; perforated material: min 30% transmittance

rear.note: if rear window is nontransparent, side mirrors on both sides required (§ 316.2954(2))

frontSide.note: same as passenger cars; reflectance max 25%

backSide.note: multipurpose passenger vehicles (truck chassis or off-road features, 10 persons or fewer); reflectance max 35%

rear.note: dual side mirrors required if nontransparent

tint.measuredHow: film + glass combined (applied to and tested on the glass of the specific vehicle; 'transmittance' includes glazing)
tint.dualMirrors: Required if the rear window is made nontransparent (§ 316.2954(2), mirrors per § 316.294).
tint.certificateOrSticker: Installer must affix a nonremovable compliance label on the inside left door jamb stating compliance, trade name of the material and installer's business name (§ 316.2955(1)).

medicalExemption.text: The Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles issues medical exemption certificates for Lupus, autoimmune diseases or other conditions requiring limited light exposure; covers windshield, side windows and windows behind the driver; tied to the vehicle (VIN, decal number), nontransferable; a fee may be charged.

penalty.text: Driver/owner: noncriminal traffic infraction, nonmoving violation under ch. 318 (base $30 under § 318.18(2) plus added fees/court costs). Selling or installing illegal material: second-degree misdemeanor.

quotes: a total solar reflectance of visible light of not more than 25 percent as measured on the nonfilm side and a light transmittance of at least 28 percent in the visible light range.
a total solar reflectance of visible light of not more than 35 percent as measured on the nonfilm side and a light transmittance of at least 15 percent in the visible light range
a light transmittance of at least 6 percent in the visible light range may be used on multipurpose passenger vehicles.
Every percentage measurement required by ss. 316.2951-316.2954 is subject to a tolerance of plus or minus 3 percent.

Sunscreening material along a strip at the top of the windshield, so long as such material is transparent and does not encroach upon the driver’s direct forward viewing area ... AS/1 portion of the windshield.

helmet.conditions: Riders over 21 may ride without a helmet if covered by an insurance policy with at least $10,000 in medical benefits for motorcycle crash injuries; eye protection required for operators.

handheldPhone.noviceOrAgeBan: Handheld use banned for all drivers in school crossings, school zones and active work zones (§ 316.306)
handheldPhone.fineText: Texting: first offense noncriminal nonmoving infraction (base $30, § 318.18(2)); second within 5 years: moving violation. School/work zone handheld: moving violation, 3 points.

radarDetector.note: commercial vehicles over 10,001 lb banned federally (49 CFR 392.71)

underglow.rule: No lamp showing red, red and white, or blue light visible from directly in front; blue lights reserved to police and certain authorized vehicles (§ 316.2397). No specific underglow statute.

liftHeight.rule: Max bumper height (ground to bottom of bumper) by net weight: cars <2,500 lb 22 in front/22 in rear; 2,500-3,499 lb 24/26; 3,500+ lb 27/29. Trucks <2,000 lb 24/26; 2,000-3,000 lb 27/29; 3,000-5,000 lb 28/30. Vehicles over 5,000 lb net shipping weight not covered.

openQuestions: Studded tires: § 316.299 bans roughened wheels 'other than roughened pneumatic rubber tires having studs designed to improve traction without materially injuring the surface of the highway' - reads as an exception, so 'restricted' (not an outright ban as often reported).
Total fine amount for a tint ticket varies by county (base $30 + § 318.18 surcharges); no single max figure in statute.
Medical exemption: official FLHSMV application page URL not verified; statute URL given.
Statute links point to the 2025 Florida Statutes; the 2026 edition was checked for 316.2953/316.2954/316.305 and shows identical text and history.
